content: The ADP-ribosylation factor-binding protein GGA1 is a protein encoded by the GGA1 gene in humans. This gene belongs to the Golgi-localized, gamma adaptin ear-containing, ARF-binding (GGA) protein family. Proteins in this family are coat proteins that are widely distributed and play a critical role in regulating the trafficking of proteins between the trans-Golgi network and the lysosome. GGA1 contains an amino-terminal VHS (Vps27, Hrs, and STAM) domain, which is responsible for mediating the sorting of mannose 6-phosphate receptors at the trans-Golgi network. Additionally, it has a carboxy-terminal region that is homologous to the ear domain of gamma-adaptins. This structural organization is essential for its function in protein trafficking. Multiple alternatively spliced transcript variants of the GGA1 gene have been identified, which encode different isoforms of the protein. GGA1 has been demonstrated to interact with several other proteins, including Sortilin 1, BACE2 (Beta-site APP-cleaving enzyme 2), RABEP1 (Rabaptin, RAB GTPase binding effector protein 1), and ARF3 (ADP-ribosylation factor 3). These interactions suggest its involvement in various cellular processes related to protein sorting and trafficking.
